item.title: 莫斯科附近的一座仓库着火。乌克兰无人机机组人员准备再次发动袭击
item.description:
夜间，一波又一波的乌克兰无人机袭击了莫斯科郊外的大型物流中心。第二天早上，俄罗斯最大的零售仓库之一仍然熊熊燃烧，黑烟升腾到天空。
数百英里外，乌克兰无人机机组人员在完成一晚的工作后几乎没有停下来，就开始准备另一次袭击。
一小群士兵迅速集结在乌克兰南部的一片向日葵田里，聚集了大约 20 架装有炸药的小型飞机无人机，然后将它们发射到俄罗斯。
美联社记者团队观察了周日上午乌克兰第 413“突袭”无人系统团的发射——这是对乌克兰战争努力迅速扩大的一部分的罕见观察。
这是乌克兰的最新策略——远程无人机旨在将战争深入俄罗斯境内，攻击远离前线的军事、工业和后勤场所。
基辅今年加大了对俄罗斯的攻击力度，使用远程导弹和大量无人机瞄准军事工业和能源设施。它还对巨型Wildberry 仓库进行了越来越多的打击，烧毁了这家俄罗斯在线零售巨头价值数十亿美元的商品。
在莫斯科全面入侵乌克兰近 4.5 年后，这些袭击让俄罗斯公众重新认识了这场战争。袭击的规模还迫使俄罗斯军方将防空范围扩展到更大的地区，扰乱了机场，引发了燃料短缺，并削弱了俄罗斯的士气。
该团指挥官叶夫亨·卡拉斯 (Yevhen Karas) 表示，他的部队还在几个小时前参与了对莫斯科以南约 45 公里（28 英里）处的野莓仓库的袭击，这是乌克兰迄今为止对俄罗斯最大规模的袭击之一。
卡拉斯说，“如果我们想要获得稳定、长期的和平，以及正常的和平”，乌克兰就需要惩罚克里姆林宫。
他补充说，“他们的伤亡越大”，他们就会越早寻求和平。
基辅官员的目标是让俄罗斯公众感受到战争的后果，并向俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京施压，要求其谈判和平解决方案。到目前为止，普京还没有表现出他打算结束战争的迹象。
然而，卡拉斯认为，乌克兰的远程打击行动对俄罗斯经济的影响正在让俄罗斯普通民众认识到战争的代价，并希望这将促使莫斯科在美国斡旋的双方谈判陷入僵局数月后重返谈判桌。
周日早上，在无人机升空之前，卡拉斯拿出一支黑色记号笔，在机身上写下一条信息：“莫斯科在天空下燃烧，红色火焰升得如此温暖和高高，黑烟在城镇上空移动，火光照亮了周围的夜晚。”
与大多数乌克兰现役军人一样，卡拉斯在 2022 年 2 月 24 日俄罗斯入侵乌克兰之前过着截然不同的生活。
但那天，38岁的大学主修哲学的他和他的兄弟弗拉基米尔双双志愿奔赴前线。他的兄弟在保卫基辅地区时被杀。在接下来的几个月里，卡拉斯晋升为乌克兰特种作战部队的一名军官。
2024 年，卡拉斯被任命为新组建的第 413 突袭无人系统团的指挥官，该团最初是一支使用无人机执行侦察和其他战场任务的部队。
随着无人机技术的发展和飞行距离从数百英里增加到一千多英里，他的部队的任务是使用乌克兰国产 FP-1 无人机对俄罗斯深处的目标进行远程行动。
该部门的其他成员包括一名前歌剧歌手、一名电脑程序员、一名说唱歌手和一名大提琴手。他们的日常工作现在集中在一系列非常简单的任务上：准备无人机、检查系统、将其移动到位并发射。
该部队的奖章——世界各地的军队称之为“挑战硬币”——一侧带有部队的徽章，是一支风格化的三爪箭头。另一幅是克里姆林宫在火焰中的浮雕，一架无人机飞过其上空。
卡拉斯表示，在战争的现阶段，莫斯科应该敬畏天空。
卡拉斯说：“莫斯科人应该在他们美妙的地铁里过夜，就像基辅居民多年来一直在地下躲避俄罗斯导弹和无人机袭击一样。”
回到向日葵田，无人机升空后，士兵们就收拾好装备开走了，几乎没有留下任何活动痕迹。

item.title: 卡米拉女王希望她能在访问癌症慈善机构时分享国王的诊断结果
item.description:
伦敦（美联社）——英国女王卡米拉表示，她在丈夫的癌症诊断结果公开宣布前几天就知道了，并发现在那段时间访问癌症中心时很难不谈论他的病情。
国王查理三世于 2024 年 2 月 5 日宣布，他正在接受一种未公开的癌症治疗，这打破了王室将健康问题保密的传统。国王公开谈论他的诊断结果被认为说服了更多的男性接受前列腺癌和其他形式的疾病检查。
女王表示，在宣布查尔斯的诊断结果一周前，她在伦敦皇家自由医院开设了玛吉癌症支持中心，当时她“渴望”谈论查尔斯的诊断，但她知道自己不能。卡米拉自 2008 年起担任 Maggie’s 总裁，该公司在英国 27 家医院运营癌症中心。
“当时没有人能说什么。那是相当困难的，”卡米拉在周三发布的纪念该慈善机构成立 30 周年的视频中说道。“我几乎要说什么，但你知道，我觉得现在还不是说的时候。”
最近有关国王的最新消息称，随着他继续接受癌症治疗，他的健康状况正在朝着积极的方向发展。
卡米拉的八分钟视频是根据女王和玛吉首席执行官劳拉·李之间的对话改编的，劳拉·李表示，自从国王宣布确诊以来，参观该慈善机构中心的男性人数增加了 12%。
玛吉提供信息、咨询和其他形式的支持，帮助癌症患者克服恐惧，在接受治疗的同时继续生活。
卡米拉说，在查尔斯确诊后，她更好地理解了对此类服务的需求。
“看看我的丈夫，没有什么能阻止他，”她说。“他只是说，‘这是我的方式。我会应对它。’”

item.title: 以色列军方对 Hind Rajab 和巴勒斯坦护理人员被杀事件展开刑事调查
item.description:
JERUSALEM (AP) — Israel’s military on Wednesday announced its first criminal investigations into troop conduct inGaza, focusing on the killings of 5-year-old Hind Rajab and her family and of 15 Palestinian paramedics.
The military said it would not probe three other attacks that killed aid workers fromWorld Central Kitchenand Doctors Without Borders. It said it had completed reviews of 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and made decisions on the five cases.
Chef José Andrés, founder of U.S.-based World Central Kitchen, condemned the decision on X as “wrong and painful.”
The investigations involve killings that drew a heavy international outcry. Hind was trapped in a vehicle with her slain relatives, pleading for help by phone before she too was killed in February 2024. After the shooting of the15 medics in March 2025, troops bulldozed their bodies into a mass grave.
Israel’s campaign in Gaza has killed more than 73,000 people, including tens of thousands of women and children, according to the territory’s Health Ministry. Rights groups and U.N. commissions have said the campaign amounts to genocide and that Israeli forces have committed a litany of war crimes, including indiscriminate use of force and deliberate killings of civilians.
Israel denies accusations of genocide and war crimes and says it is targeting Hamas after its October 2023 attack on southern Israel. It blames civilian deaths on Hamas because the militant group operates in populated areas in the tiny, overcrowded strip.
Israeli officials contend the country’s justice system can address any violations by its troops, but rights groups say soldiers are almost never held accountable.
Wednesday’s statement did not mention many other high-profile killings that Israel has pledged to investigate, such as itsstrikes on a hospital in southern Gazathat killed five journalists in August 2025, including Mariam Dagga, a visual journalist who freelanced for The Associated Press and other news organizations.
Hind’s grandmother, also named Hind Rajab, told the AP by phone that the Israeli investigation into her killing is not enough.
“An international investigation is required to uncover the truth and hold all those responsible accountable,” she said. “We call for justice, not only for Hind, but for all Gaza children.”
The military in Wednesday’s statement admitted to firing at the car carrying the 5-year-old, four of her cousins and her aunt and uncle as they fled an Israeli invasion of Gaza City.
As gunfire sprayed around them, the girl’s cousin, 15-year-old Layan Hamada, called the Palestinian Red Crescent paramedic center, telling staff there her family had been killed. Seconds later, more gunshots were heard, and Layan’s screaming stopped, according tothe Red Crescent recordingof the call.
Palestinian paramedics dispatched an ambulance to rescue Hind and stayed on the line with her until contact was lost. Hind, her five relatives and two medics from the ambulancewere found dead12 days later.
The military admitted Wednesday that troops had fired toward that ambulance, killing the two medics.
Dyab Abou Jahjah, director of the Belgium-based Hind Rajab foundation, told Al-Jazeera he considered the military investigations a “charade meant to whitewash the culprits instead of convicting them.”
The Palestinian Red Crescent also insists on an international investigation, according to Raed al-Nims, a spokesman for the organization in Gaza. “Israeli measures are not enough,” he told the AP.
A movie docudrama about Hind’s death, “The Voice of Hind Rajab,” won international awards and wasnominated for an Oscar.
In the killing of the paramedics, Israeli troops fired on an ambulance driving to retrieve casualties from an Israeli offensive in the southern city of Rafah, then fired on other emergency vehicles that came looking for the first one,according to phone footage and the sole survivor of the shootings. Fifteen medics and emergency responders from the Red Crescent and Gaza’s Civil Defense were killed.
Troops then bulldozed over the bodies and vehicles, burying them in a mass grave. U.N. and rescue workers were only able to reach the site a week later to dig out the bodies.
The Israeli military initially said it opened fire because the vehicles were “advancing suspiciously” on troops without headlights or emergency signals. But it backtracked after the footage emerged, showing the teams driving slowly with their emergency lights flashing and logos visible. A deputy commander was directed to step down over the killings.
“We are not obligated to prove the truth because it is already proven to the whole world,” Eid Azizi, a Palestinian Red Crescent spokesperson, told the AP in a phone call. “We shouldn’t have reached this point if they respected and followed international humanitarian law.”
The military said it had decided against a criminal investigation into April 2024 airstrikes that hit a convoy of World Central Kitchen vehicles, killing seven staffers.
The aid group, which distributes food in Gaza, said at the time it had coordinated with the military over the convoy’s movement. The vehicles, which had the group’s logo on their roofs visible from the air, were left incinerated and mangled.
Wednesday’s military statement said individuals in the vehicles were mistakenly identified as armed Hamas operatives. But it concluded that the commanders’ decisions “did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct.” At the time, two officers were removed from their positions and three others reprimanded.
World Central Kitchen responded in a statement saying the military’s account of the strike was untrue, “conflates different timelines and events, muddies the story and shifts the blame.” It called for an independent investigation.
The military also decided not to take criminal action over the killings of four staffers from Doctors Without Borders in two separate instances in November 2023 and February 2024.
Military investigators will now take up the probes and present their findings to military prosecutors. The military advocate general can then decide to keep investigating, indict any soldiers involved or decline to charge them.
Any action will take a long time, if it comes at all, said Tal Steiner, head of the Israeli rights group HaMoked.
Indictments are very uncommon and convictions even more so, she said, recalling only one soldier who had spent time behind bars since Oct. 7, 2023, for alleged abuse of Palestinian prisoners. That soldier was imprisoned for seven months under a June 2025 plea bargain.
“It’s very rare that soldiers accused of harming Palestinians even go to court ... and even rarer that they get a severe punishment,” Steiner said.
Just 0.17% of all military investigations launched during three Gaza operations from 2014 to 2022 led to prosecution, according to an analysis by Israeli rights group Yesh Din.
The war began on Oct. 7, 2023, when Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people, mostly civilians, in southern Israel and abducted 251 others.
Israeli strikes have continued in Gaza since a ceasefire deal came into effect in October, killing at least 1,270 people, according to the Health Ministry.
The ministry, part of the Hamas-led government, maintains detailed casualty records that are seen as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and independent experts. It does not give a breakdown of civilians and militants but says women and children constitute about half of the dead. ___
Magdy reported from Cairo. Associated Press writer Erin Cunningham in Jerusalem contributed to this report.

item.title: 前福奇顾问承认在大流行期间密谋隐瞒 COVID-19 研究记录
item.description:
马里兰州格林贝尔特（美联社）——传染病专家安东尼·福西普博士的前高级顾问周二因密谋隐瞒与致命的 COVID-19 大流行起源研究相关的联邦记录而被判有罪。
David Morens 博士定于 11 月 12 日在马里兰州格林贝尔特由美国地区法官 Paula Xiis 宣判。莫伦斯承认密谋诈骗美国政府，这是一项重罪，最高可判处五年监禁。
“通过今天认罪，莫伦斯博士已经为自己的所作所为承担了责任，他将继续这样做，”辩护律师蒂姆·贝莱维茨在认罪听证会后的一份声明中说。
莫伦斯被指控在国家过敏和传染病研究所工作期间使用他的私人电子邮件帐户故意规避公共记录法。司法部指控他隐瞒或销毁了与 COVID-19 研究拨款相关的讨论记录，其中包括恢复一项有争议的冠状病毒拨款的努力。
该起诉书是在众议院共和党人对 COVID-19 大流行的起源进行调查之后提出的，该调查仔细审查了莫伦斯的电子邮件通讯，并指控他故意隐瞒记录。在国会作证时，莫伦斯否认试图使用他的个人电子邮件规避联邦透明度法。
7 月，福奇在国会就其处理 COVID-19 大流行的听证会上多次援引第五修正案反对自证其罪的权利。上周五，在国土安全委员会的多数共和党人按照党派路线投票认定他藐视国会后，福奇拒绝了自愿出席参议院第二个小组的请求。
78 岁的莫伦斯来自马里兰州切斯特，福奇没有因此案受到指控。

item.title: 卡梅洛·安东尼寻求新审判，法官不再参与德克萨斯州田径比赛杀人案
item.description:
得克萨斯州麦金尼（美联社）——星期三，在一场重要听证会之前，主审德克萨斯州少年卡梅洛·安东尼谋杀案的法官被撤回此案，听证会决定是否对一名 17 岁运动员在高中田径比赛中被刺死的事件进行新的审判。
对于现年 19 岁的安东尼来说，免职是一次法律上的胜利，他的律师希望法官在 6 月份的审判后停止审理此案，部分原因是法官在一次电视采访中表示，陪审员在对奥斯汀·梅特卡夫被杀一案做出有罪判决时“做得对”。
这张由德克萨斯州刑事司法部于 2026 年 8 月 18 日星期二提供的预订照片显示的是卡梅洛·安东尼。（德克萨斯州刑事司法部，美联社）
被判处 35 年监禁的安东尼在达拉斯郊区的法庭上，当一名来访法官下令州地方法官约翰·罗奇回避时，他穿着绿色的监狱连身裤。法官迈克尔·奇蒂后来被指派审理此案。
麦金尼法庭外，走廊里爆发出欢呼声，一些安东尼的支持者高呼“释放卡梅洛！”在停车场。
安东尼的律师在一份声明中表示：“今天的裁决回答了一个基本问题：一个理性、充分知情的观察者是否会看到罗奇法官的行为，并相信他可以公平、公正地考虑重新审判的动议。”
周四，安东尼预计将返回法庭参加听证会，以确定是否需要重审。
今年夏天，陪审员驳回了安东尼去年在体育场露天看台与梅特卡夫对峙时出于自卫的主张。安东尼在审判期间没有出庭作证。其他出庭的学生描述了安东尼在春雨中拒绝离开梅特卡夫团队的帐篷引发的激烈争执。
该案引起了全国关注，部分原因是大量社交媒体帖子以种族术语放大了这起杀戮事件。安东尼是黑人；梅特卡夫是白人。然而，双方律师都告诉陪审员，这场悲剧与种族无关。
安东尼的法律团队辩称，需要重审，部分原因是罗奇执行了严格的法庭规则，他们称这些规则限制了公众参与诉讼程序。他们周三还关注了罗奇在审判结束后向达拉斯一家电视台发表的评论。
在听证会开始时播放的采访中，罗奇被问及陪审团是否“正确”。
“是的，他们做到了，”罗奇说，并补充道：“无论他们说什么，他们都是对的。”
2026 年 8 月 19 日星期三，科林县法院位于德克萨斯州麦金尼。（Elías Valverde II/《达拉斯晨报》，美联社）
2026 年 8 月 19 日星期三，德克萨斯州麦金尼，法官小约翰·罗奇 (John Roach Jr.) 被回避参加安东尼谋杀案下一阶段的审判，卡梅洛·安东尼 (Karmelo Anthony) 的支持者在科林县法院外庆祝。（Elías Valverde II/《达拉斯晨报》，美联社）
在采访中，罗奇还为自己的法庭规则进行了辩护，并谈到了有关此案的网上帖子的冲击。
来访的法官西德·哈勒表示，他不认识罗奇，他相信罗奇在重审听证会上会是公平的，但考虑到其他人可能会觉得这件事，他同意辩方回避的请求。哈尔在书面命令中表示，证据表明法官的“公正性可能会受到合理质疑”，并命令另一名法官“主持所有进一步的诉讼程序”。
裁决后，罗奇没有立即回应置评请求。
检察官比尔·维尔斯基敦促法庭保留罗奇。他说法官“没有做错任何事”，他的法庭规则是为了保护审判的公正性，这导致示威者离开法院。裁决后，威尔斯基没有立即回应置评请求。
去年，随着全国对这起杀戮事件的关注加剧，梅特卡夫和安东尼的家人表示，他们一直是骚扰的目标。
“我们都收到了死亡威胁，”威尔斯基说。
当安东尼坐在纪念高中看台上的帐篷下时，几所学校正在比赛。目击者作证称，梅特卡夫和其他人多次要求安东尼离开，导致冲突升级。
检察官称安东尼挑衅了梅特卡夫，目击者作证称安东尼是侵略者。
据警方报告称，安东尼有一次把手伸进一个袋子里，回答道：“摸摸我，看看会发生什么。”
据目击者称，梅特卡夫推了安东尼，安东尼随后拔出一把刀刺伤了他的胸部。
美联社撰稿人吉姆·韦尔图诺对奥斯汀的这篇报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 圣地亚哥县将停止让联邦移民代理在当地射击场进行训练
item.description:
出于对特朗普政府暴力镇压移民的担忧，南加州一个县将停止让联邦移民当局在当地射击场进行训练。
圣地亚哥县监管人员周二以 3 比 2 投票决定终止与移民和海关执法局以及海关和边境保护局的合同，以在墨西哥边境附近的一个县拥有的设施和该县租用的一个海军设施进行培训。在繁忙的美墨边境进行移民执法、海关和移民检查的机构多年来一直签订在这些设施进行培训的合同。
“联邦移民代理在当地和全国范围内以多种不同方式伤害了我们的社区，”投票终止合同的监管人员之一莫妮卡·蒙哥马利·斯特佩 (Monica Montgomery Steppe) 说。“我们只是不想成为其中的同谋。”
圣地亚哥县当选警长凯利·马丁内斯 (Kelly Martinez) 在投票后表示，她告诉 ICE 不再有权使用该县的设施，并称她“经过数月的对话并听取了社区对 ICE 特工在该国其他地区武装对抗期间行动的担忧”后做出了这一决定。
但马丁内斯表示，美国海关与边境保护局可能会继续使用县设施，与同样当选的监管人员摊牌。治安官对美国海关边境保护局打击边境犯罪和促进贸易和旅行的工作进行了长时间的辩护。
马丁内斯说：“终止美国海关与边境保护局使用该设施的决定将会伤害边境两侧太多的人。”“作为警长，我有责任保护和服务所有居住或进入圣地亚哥县的人。”
在居民呼吁美墨边境这个拥有超过 300 万人口的县终止合同后，监管机构进行了投票。他们表示，这将是停止帮助特朗普政府大规模驱逐运动的一种方式，该运动导致家庭分裂，并导致联邦特工与从明尼苏达州到缅因州等社区的居民之间发生致命冲突。
其他社区，包括附近的埃斯孔迪多市以及纽约和明尼苏达州的其他社区，也讨论了是否允许移民代理使用他们的射击场，但选择保持合同不变。
投票反对此举的圣地亚哥县主管吉姆·德斯蒙德表示，执法机构应该共同工作和培训，让特工走得更远去接受培训不会有任何效果。
“ICE 已经越界了，但你如何解决这个问题？你可以​​通过更多的培训来解决这个问题，”他说。
海关和边境保护局局长罗德尼·斯科特表示，该机构依靠该县的射击场来培训 1,700 名警察。他说，如果没有它，他就会把他们送到其他地方接受强制性枪械训练，这将减少当地人员配置，并影响跨越美墨边境的贸易和旅行。
斯科特在一份声明中表示：“圣地亚哥县监事会等当地合作伙伴故意破坏边境安全并使我们的社区面临风险，这是史无前例的。”
在圣地亚哥，CBP 自 2017 年起就已达成协议，使用该县的培训中心，ICE 自 2021 年起也已达成协议。根据提议终止合同的监管人员的一封信，自 2024 年以来，联邦特工已在该中心接受了 3,300 多个小时的培训。
信中称，自 2022 年以来，ICE 还达成协议，使用该县在米拉马尔海军陆战队航空站租赁的海军拥有的射击场。
投票终止合同的圣地亚哥官员表示，他们希望保持该地区移民社区的信任，并努力区分当地警察和联邦移民代理。支持者表示，特朗普政府已责成其他联邦机构帮助执行移民执法，由于当局戴着口罩和便服，很难知道他们为哪个机构工作。
“我们的社区是一个家，而不是一个目标，”董事会主席泰拉·劳森-雷默 (Terra Lawson-Remer) 本周表示。她是提议终止合同的两名主管之一。“如果特朗普政府想在这项法律和驱逐议程上花费数十亿美元，他们可以使用自己的联邦资源来实施。”

item.title: 检察官表示，科米的贝壳帖子可能被解读为特朗普的威胁，“没有严重争议”
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The Department of Justice is defending itsprosecution of former FBI Director James Comey, saying “there is no serious dispute” that a social media post of seashells he made last year could be understood as a threat againstPresident Donald Trump.
Prosecutors also called into question Comey’s account that he had found the seashells in the numerical arrangement of “86 47” while walking on a beach in North Carolina and suggested that his May 2025 post on Instagram was an effort to generate attention for a forthcoming novel about a social media personality whose words inspire his fans to attack his foes.
The arguments in motionslate Tuesday represent the government’s most detailed explanation of its indictment and were filed in response towide-ranging defense efforts to dismiss the caseon grounds including that it constitutes a vindictive prosecution and that Comey’s post did not amount to a true threat. Comey’s lawyers contend that investigators in the case misled judges, submitted documents containing false statements, withheld key facts and repeatedly came up empty in their efforts to prove that Comey intended a physical threat or knew that the number 86 could suggest violence.
The U.S. Department of Justice logo is seen on a podium before a news conference, May 4, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson, File)
The entry for “86”from Merriam-Webster, the dictionary used by The Associated Press, says its meaning is “to throw out,” “to get rid of” or “to refuse service to.” Trump, a Republican, is the 47th president.
Federal prosecutors maintain that the photo of the seashells, which Comey said he found on the beach, constituted a threat against Trump. Comey deleted the post shortly after he put it up, saying he did not know that anyone interpreted the numbers as a call to violence. His lawyers have said that the slogan has long meant to “get rid of” or “eject” and has been featured on thousands of items sold online and regularly displayed at protests.
The Justice Department defends the James Comey prosecution in the Trump threat case. AP correspondent Mike Hempen has the latest.
But the department sought in its filings to place the post against the backdrop ofassassination plots or attemptsagainst Trump in the months before and after Comey’s post. Prosecutors say that two minutes before the post was made, Comey’s wife texted him a screenshot of a definition of “86” that said “to get rid of or refuse service.”
“There is no serious dispute that an objective viewer of Comey’s post could read it to mean ‘Kill President Trump,’” prosecutors wrote.
A portrait of President Donald Trump is displayed at the Justice Department building in Washington, June 2, 2026. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite, File)
The photo was posted days before Comey was set to release a novel he wrote titled “FDR Drive,” in which a prosecutor pursues a far-right social media personality who has called out his adversaries by name and inspired violence against them by his fans, the department said.
After the Instagram post provoked an outcry, according to the government’s filings, Comey’s publishing agent observed in a text message to him that he had “gone viral.” Comey responded that that was “not my intention, but I’ll be OK if it sells books.” The agent replied, ”Music to an agent’s ears.”
Prosecutors also asserted there was “reason to doubt” Comey’s account of having come upon the seashells while on a walk, saying they were located 4 miles (6 kilometers) “down from the beach from beachfront property where Comey was staying, in an area separated from the ocean by a sand dune.” They said there was “no evidence that anyone else arranged, photographed, or even saw the shells.”
Comey’s lawyers have called the indictment,which was filed months after an earlier and unrelated case against him was dismissed, part of a Trump retribution campaigntargeting one of the president’s vocal critics. Trumpfired Comey as head of the FBIin 2017 as Comey was overseeing an investigation into potential ties between Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign and Russia. Trump since then has called for him and other perceived adversaries to be jailed.
But the Justice Department denied allegations of vindictiveness, saying the decision to indict Comey was made by the U.S. attorney in the area and did not stem from a directive from the president or the attorney general.
To bolster their claims that Comey was unjustly targeted, the defense team argued that investigators struggled to develop compelling evidence from witnesses that Comey had intended the post as a threat, but they concealed that from federal magistrates as they applied for warrants to search digital accounts associated with Comey and his wife
For instance, defense lawyers have said that the FBI searched an internal database of information about open and closed investigations for any indication of an association between Comey and the term “86” but found inconclusive results. An FBI agent also requested a review of the FBI file for the case against reputed mobster John Gambino, which Comey worked on as a young prosecutor, but found no references to the term “86.”
Investigators also interviewed a key government cooperator in the case, Salvatore “Sammy the Bull” Gravano, who said he did not recall ever discussing the term “86” with Comey or hearing it in connection with the trial.
The latest filings made clear that the administration was standing behind the premise of the case.
“No Government theory was disproved at that time, or now. No intentionally false omission exists, much less one made with reckless disregard for the truth,” prosecutors wrote.
“The evidence still supports that Defendant acted at least recklessly by consciously disregarding a substantial risk that his coded message of ‘8647’ that he sent to his 200,000 or so Instagram followers, and the millions of secondary social media users who would view this as threatening violence against the President of the United States,” they added.

item.title: 肯尼迪中心告诉法庭，不会在 9 月 8 日之前尝试恢复特朗普的名字
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——肯尼迪中心已向联邦法院表示，至少在 9 月 8 日之前，随着围绕该表演艺术场馆未来的另一场法律战即将展开，它不会试图将唐纳德·特朗普总统的名字重新印在大楼的正面。
在周二晚间提交的一份状态报告中，此举的反对者表示，肯尼迪中心与特朗普结盟的董事会成员“似乎有意”藐视早些时候法院要求将共和党总统的名字从大楼中删除的命令。肯尼迪中心表示，“最早”要到劳动节之后才会推进这些计划，以便有时间进行法律论证。
俄亥俄州民主党众议员乔伊斯·贝蒂 (Joyce Beatty) 是该委员会的当然成员，他的律师向美国地区法官克里斯托弗·库珀 (Christopher Cooper) 施压，要求其早日做出裁决，称“有充分理由相信，被告将在 9 月 8 日之后尽早尝试实施这项最新非法决议的部分或部分内容。”
本月举行的一次董事会会议原本预计将主要集中讨论关闭肯尼迪中心进行翻修的选择，但结果却变成了另一次推动将特朗普的名字贴在这座建筑上的努力，这是总统及其支持者在美国首都留下实体印记的海外行动的一部分。
董事会通过了一项决议，以特朗普的名字命名大楼前的广场，并将他的名字添加到场馆的正面，这样上面就会写着“由唐纳德·J·特朗普总统修复和翻新的约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心”。比蒂在文件中表示，如果特朗普肯尼迪中心基金达到 1 亿美元，董事会还同意增加对总统的额外提及。
在这种情况下，立面将写着“由唐纳德·J·特朗普总统修复和翻新的约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心，由特朗普·肯尼迪中心基金资助”。
董事会还投票支持关闭两年进行翻修，而该机构的一些标志性节目，包括肯尼迪中心荣誉奖和马克·吐温美国幽默奖，将在场外地点举行。国家交响乐团本周宣布，即将到来的演出季将在华盛顿及其周边的六个演出场地进行。
库珀五月裁定，贴在大楼上的写有特朗普名字的字母是非法添加的，他下令将其拆除，但政府未能说服法院推翻这一决定。从那时起，曾经安装这些字母的区域就被防水布覆盖了，这让那些试图从大楼上抹去总统名字的人感到沮丧。
在最新的文件中，肯尼迪中心没有承诺拆除防水布，称覆盖物的安装是为了方便删除特朗普的名字，并且是“对屋顶悬挑进行水测试和结构修复”所需的更广泛系统的一部分。
更广泛地说，比蒂的律师诺姆·艾森 (Norm Eisen) 和纳撒尼尔·泽林斯基 (Nathaniel Zelinsky) 对董事会本月投票的公正性提出了质疑，这与库珀在 3 月份呼吁关闭这座大楼的投票“信息不灵通且似乎是注定的”时提出的担忧相呼应。
在八月份的会议之前，肯尼迪中心的管理层表示，将向董事会提供三种选择，包括完全关闭或部分关闭，以允许“在不受工作影响的空间中继续进行一些公共访问和有限的活动”。第三种选择是“考虑一系列高度有限的分阶段关闭，以仅满足该中心最严重的基础设施需求，同时安排和维护全部项目。”
在周二的文件中，肯尼迪中心表示，达美咨询集团的一位分析师得出的结论是，部分关闭将在四年内完成，“将增加施工时间和成本，并导致严重的安全问题。”
肯尼迪中心表示，该分析师“建议董事会全面关闭两年，这将最大限度地降低总成本，最大限度地缩短节目因施工而受到干扰的时间，并最好地维护该中心作为世界级表演艺术场所的声誉。”
然而，艾森和泽林斯基指出，材料是在会议前两天才提供给董事会的。他们表示，一些文件似乎是在库珀 5 月裁决之前创建的，并提到肯尼迪中心的关闭最初定于 7 月 6 日生效。
比蒂的律师辩称，八月份关闭肯尼迪中心的投票“表现出了与第一次投票相同的缺陷”。

item.title: 国家安全问题在南卡罗来纳州辩论中困扰参议员达林·格雷厄姆
item.description:
南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚（美联社）——参议员达林·格雷厄姆在周二晚上的一场关于外交政策的基本问题的辩论中失利，这是她已故哥哥的标志性问题。在她面临决选的一周前，这是她为保住上个月被任命的南卡罗来纳州席位而犯下的一个引人注目的失误。
政治新手格雷厄姆被问及美国在台湾和南中国海是否有国家安全利益——这是民主党和共和党政府长期以来的争论。她努力回答，然后才承认“国家安全不是我的事”。
“我对国家安全不太了解，”她补充道。
她在下周共和党提名决选中的对手众议员拉尔夫·诺曼表示，答案表明格雷厄姆没有资格担任这一角色。
“根据她的选择，她将竞选美国参议院议员。任期六年，”诺曼说。“你需要完全熟悉你将要处理的问题。这不是在职培训，你不能那样做。”
这一时刻与格雷厄姆的弟弟林赛 (Lindsey) 形成了鲜明的对比，林赛于 7 月 11 日意外去世。这也为诺曼这位老牌保守派政治家提供了新的攻击途径，因为他试图在唐纳德·特朗普总统的第一次竞选中击败唐纳德·特朗普总统对格雷厄姆的支持。这位共和党总统定于周五访问南卡罗来纳州为她竞选。
在参议院任职的几十年里，林赛·格雷厄姆因其参与外交政策而闻名，他进行了无数次的出访，有时作为美国立法者小组的一员与国际领导人会面并亲眼观察有争议的领域。
曾多次前往台湾，包括2022年率领代表团进行为期两天的访问，其中包括与台湾总统蔡英文和台湾国防部长会面。
达林·格雷厄姆被问到：“台湾和南中国海是美国的国家安全问题吗？如果是，为什么或如何？”
格雷厄姆避免直接回应，而是提到了她哥哥丰富的经验以及她以不同方式领导的愿望。
“我哥哥在空军服役了 33 年，所以我会尽我所能来支持军队，”格雷厄姆说。她经常在笔记本上阅读笔记，笔记上的纸页挂在讲台前面。“我父亲在军队。我在这里不是一个优雅的政治家；国家安全不是我的事，不是我的专业领域，但我确实支持军队。”
候选人不允许在辩论中做笔记，但格雷厄姆在广播开始前花了几分钟在她的便笺簿上写下了很多内容。诺曼写下了一些东西，但没有那么广泛。
作为临时参议员，格雷厄姆周围都是她哥哥在国会山的许多工作人员，其中许多人在国内外问题上与他共事多年。她多次感谢他们让她了解立法问题，并指出她在工作的几周时间是富有成效的，在这段时间里她让立法获得了通过，其中包括一项以她哥哥命名的俄罗斯制裁法案。
在她哥哥去世后，格雷厄姆多次被问及她将如何进一步或转变他对国家安全的强烈关注，这种态度是他参议院投资组合的本质。
辩论结束后，当记者问她是否想再次回答主持人的问题时，她加倍努力，表示她更关注南卡罗来纳州人的日常问题。
“老实说，他们更担心自己的钱包，而不是南海，”格雷厄姆说。“所以这将是我最大的关注点。”
格雷厄姆补充说，她在辩论中多次谈到中国构成的整体国家安全威胁。
“我意识到国家安全非常重要，”格雷厄姆说。“今晚我可能在上面说了十遍中国有多糟糕，他们对我们构成了国家威胁。”
台湾经常成为中国侵略和国际社会支持其自治权利的导火索。美国对于如果大陆入侵是否会在军事上保卫台湾方面保持战略模糊政策，但几代人以来一直致力于加强台湾的防御。
中国宣称台湾是其领土的一部分，它位于南中国海全球贸易路线沿线，尽管2016年根据1982年《联合国海洋法公约》做出的仲裁裁决宣告北京的广泛主张无效，但中国实际上对所有海域都拥有主权。
美国特种作战司令部司令弗兰克·布拉德利上将本周访问马尼拉期间表示，美国特种作战部队已准备好与菲律宾和亚洲其他国家加强战备演习，以进一步加强安全联盟，帮助遏制该地区发生重大冲突。
可以通过 http://x.com/MegKinnardAP 联系 Meg Kinnard。

item.title: 副手试图在科罗拉多训练时向迪昂·桑德斯送达民事文件，但教练不在场
item.description:
上周，博尔德县治安官办公室的一名副手出现在科罗拉多大学校园，向迪昂·桑德斯送达民事文件，而当时教练正在公开训练，无法接近。
治安官办公室发言人周三表示，该警官被告知，布法罗队教练“当时无法收到文件收据”。据《今日美国》报道，桑德斯将被传唤作证，这是涉及他儿子希洛的破产审判的一部分，该审判将于 8 月 31 日开始。
科罗拉多州体育部门没有提供更多信息。水牛队将于 9 月 3 日在佐治亚理工学院拉开赛季序幕。
8月11日上午10点22分，这名副手带着民事文件抵达校园。那天，水牛队举行了公开训练，并制定了具体规则，观察到的任何情况都不能报告、发布或分享。
治安官办公室的高级通讯专家卡丽·哈弗菲尔德（Carrie Haverfield）在给美联社的电子邮件中写道，民事文件需要多次尝试送达的情况并不罕见。
哈弗菲尔德写道：“在与大学工作人员合作寻找更好的时间来完成这一过程时，我们从桑德斯先生的法律顾问那里得知，他们能够代表桑德斯先生收到文件收据，但是，他们不在博尔德县，所以我们将文件转移到丹佛进行送达。”“我们没有发现任何大学工作人员试图阻止公务员，相反，他们试图帮助我们的副手找到更好的时机这样做。我们不会透露我们所送达的民事文件的具体内容。”
希洛·桑德斯 (Shilo Sanders) 因高中时与保安发生的事件而引发的诉讼仍在诉讼中。该警卫对桑德斯提起诉讼，并因桑德斯缺席出庭而被判缺席判决。
去年八月，这位在科罗拉多为他父亲效力的强硬安全卫被坦帕湾海盗队裁掉。

item.title: 前温布尔登决赛选手尼克·克耶高斯因可卡因检测呈阳性而被停赛
item.description:
日内瓦（美联社）——前温布尔登决赛选手尼克·克耶高斯周三透露，他的可卡因检测呈阳性，并称兴奋剂案件给他敲响了警钟，因为伤病使他的职业生涯脱轨，他感到“无助和孤独”。
这位纪律记录不佳的31岁澳大利亚选手自2022年巅峰赛季以来仅在ATP巡回赛上打了10场单打比赛，只赢得了两场比赛，随后被暂时禁赛。随后，他进入了草地大满贯决赛，输给了诺瓦克·德约科维奇。
克耶高斯目前排名第919位。六月，他在西班牙一场低级别草地球场比赛中检测出派对毒品呈阳性。
“我最近在马略卡岛的一次药检中可卡因呈阳性，但未通过，”他在自己的 Instagram 账户上写道。“我犯了一个巨大的错误，并为此承担全部责任。”
这是这位才华横溢而又火热个性的职业生涯中最新的负面头条新闻，近年来他在球场上最引人注目的举动是去年 12 月在迪拜一场令人好奇的“性别之战”战胜阿丽娜·萨巴伦卡 (Aryna Sabalenka)。
克耶高斯面临长达四年的禁赛，但预计处罚会较轻。可卡因在比赛期间被禁止作为兴奋剂，而在比赛之外使用可卡因的处罚则较轻。
2017年的类似案件中，英国球员丹·埃文斯因在巴塞罗那公开赛上可卡因检测呈阳性而被国际网球联合会禁赛一年。
克耶高斯表示，在经历了两年的伤病之后，他很难接受职业生涯即将结束的事实。
“有时我感到无助和孤独。这些都不能成为我所做的事情的借口，”他说。他补充说，这些伤病“对我的身体和精神都造成了巨大的伤害。我的身体无法做到我的想法所期望的那样。”
克耶高斯今年单打战绩为1胜3负，上个月在温布尔登获得了双打外卡。他在第一轮中输给了搭档亚历山大·布布利克(Alexander Bublik)。
国际网球诚信机构将起诉此案，并表示该球员的样本于6月22日采集，并于7月17日在克耶高斯参加温网比赛后确认呈阳性。
ITIA 补充说，8 月 4 日实施了强制临时停职，克耶高斯并未提出上诉。
“然而，好消息是，这给我敲响了警钟，”克耶高斯写道，这表明他的职业生涯尚未结束。
“在接下来的 28 天里，我将远离社交媒体和公共生活，专注于让自己变得正确。”
克耶高斯职业生涯七个单打冠军中最近的一个是在温布尔登决赛后的第一场比赛中赢得的。2022 年 8 月，他在华盛顿特区举行的硬地赛事决赛中击败了西冈佳仁。
几周后，他进入美国公开赛四分之一决赛，输给了凯伦·卡恰诺夫。
2022 年 10 月在东京膝盖受伤后，克耶高斯在接下来的两年里只打了一次比赛，理由是手腕受伤错过了 2023 年温网。
克耶高斯在2025赛季的战绩仅为1胜4负，在澳网首轮比赛中失利，随后跳过了接下来的三项大满贯赛事。

item.title: 悉尼天鹅队因酒店不当行为和警方调查而禁止 5 名球员参加 AFL 赛季剩余比赛
item.description:
悉尼（美联社）——五名澳式足球运动员因在墨尔本一家酒店住宿期间违反球员行为准则而被悉尼天鹅队禁止参加 AFL 赛季剩余比赛，这导致警方对性侵犯指控进行调查。
天鹅队周三发表声明称，“莱利·比斯、尼克·布莱基、艾萨克·希尼、詹姆斯·乔丹和查德·华纳将不会被考虑参加 2026 年 AFL 赛季剩余比赛”，从而排除他们参加本周末的常规赛和季后赛系列赛。
天鹅队表示，俱乐部实施的制裁与维多利亚州警方的调查无关。目前还没有提出任何指控，也没有球员被认定参与涉嫌性侵犯。
周一早些时候，一名女子向东墨尔本一家酒店的工作人员投诉，警方接到报警。
天鹅队的声明称：“我们尊重维多利亚警方正在进行的调查，我们今天采取的行动与此无关。”并补充说，澳大利亚足球联盟“支持俱乐部的制裁”。
天鹅队首席执行官马修·帕夫利希在周三的新闻发布会上表示，俱乐部因一系列赛后违反行为准则的行为而受到制裁。周日比赛结束后，天鹅队的球员们住在酒店，因为商业航班无法在机场宵禁之前让球队及时返回悉尼。
“他们在外面待得很晚，他们喝酒，他们继续他们的夜晚，他们把女人带回酒店，”帕夫利奇说。这种行为“与我们对玩家的期望相差甚远。
“我们对他们要求非常高的标准。但他们远远没有达到这个标准。”
他拒绝就与警方调查有关的任何事宜发表评论。
AFL 首席执行官安德鲁·狄龙 (Andrew Dillon) 早些时候发表声明称，这些指控“令人深感担忧”。
“虽然此事仍在警方调查中，但它给我们的比赛和我们作为一项运动的责任带来了更广泛的问题，”狄龙说。“向警方报案的女性有权获得隐私和照顾，这一点应该受到尊重。”
周二晚俱乐部董事会召开会议并对相关球员进行了采访，随后出台了竞技禁令。
“悉尼天鹅队谴责对女性一切形式的虐待和不尊重行为，”天鹅队在董事会会议前的一份声明中表示。“任何冒犯或伤害他人的行为都是不可接受的，远远低于我们的期望。所有女性都应该受到尊重并感到安全。”
悉尼天鹅队主席安德鲁·普里德汉姆为球员的行为道歉，并表示俱乐部内部深感失望。
“通过做出这样的决定来有效地破坏我们的赛季，这表明我们是多么认真地对待它，”他说。

item.title: Moderna 表示其实验性 mRNA 癌症治疗通过了一项关键测试，股价飙升
item.description:
Moderna 周三宣布了一项实验性癌症治疗研究的初步结果，如果获得监管机构批准，该研究将是同类研究中的第一个，该公司股价周三上涨了一倍多。
Moderna 和默克公司正在开发一种基于 mRNA 的癌症疫苗 intismeran 的治疗方法，该疫苗旨在根据肿瘤内的独特突变为个体患者量身定制。在目前的研究中，他们将其与默克公司生产的免疫治疗药物 Keytruda 配对。
该研究比较了黑色素瘤患者同时使用 intismeran 和 Keytruda 与单独使用 Keytruda 的情况。两家公司表示，与单独使用 Keytruda 的患者相比，接受该组合治疗的患者在没有癌症复发或转移的情况下寿命更长。
两家公司没有透露患者在癌症不复发的情况下存活了多长时间，也没有透露患者的总体寿命是否更长。他们表示计划在即将召开的国际医学会议上展示研究结果。
Moderna 股价上涨超过 120%，至每股 140.12 美元。默克公司股价上涨约11%。

item.title: 债券市场的惊慌促使特朗普政府再次采取行动
item.description:
NEW YORK (AP) — Normally quiet, the bond market can occasionallysend warning signalsloud enough to hit stock markets worldwide and even grab the attention ofU.S. presidentsand other world leaders.
After the bond market’s alarm bells rose in volume through the summer, the Trump administration announced on Wednesday a move that could help calm it down. The U.S. Treasury Department said it will more than double the amount of U.S. government bonds that it will buy back, and the move worked in getting longer-term yields lower, for now at least.
Yields worldwide had earlier climbed to heights not reached in years and, in some cases, decades, because of the jump in oil prices due to thewar with Iran, worries aboutbig and growing debtsfor governments and other concerns.
The stakes are high because high yields drag on economies and bring downward pressure on stock markets after Wall Street hitrecordson excitement about big corporate profits and the promise ofartificial-intelligencetechnology.
But what’s to come is still uncertain, and some analysts warn the Treasury Department’s move could even ultimately backfire.
Here’s a look at what’s going on and how things got this way:
In the United States, the centerpiece of the bond market recently touched its highest yield in more than a year. The 10-year Treasury yield, which shows how much interest investors want the U.S. government to pay them before they’ll lend it money for a decade, topped 4.70%, before falling back to 4.65% Wednesday.
That’s up from just 3.97% before the Iran war began in late February, and it’s a significant move for the bond market.
More notably, the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield has jumped well above 5%, back to where it was in 2007, before the 2008 financial crisis sent yields crashing toward zero worldwide.
In Japan, the yield on the 10-year government bond has touched its highest level in nearly 30 years, while the German 10-year yield is back to where it was in 2011.
When the U.S. and other governments have to pay more in interest to borrow money, so do people and companies.
For many U.S. households, that’s most easily seen throughrates for mortgages. Such rates have climbed with the 10-year Treasury yield since the Iran war began, and the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage is near its highest level in a year.
Higher yields also make it more expensive for U.S. companies to borrow money to build factories and otherwise grow. That’s particularly dangerous at this moment, when big investments in data centers to power AI are amajor driver of the U.S. economy’s growth.
If high yields slow the economy, that puts pressure on the stocks. An economic slowdown would threaten how much profit companies can make, which is the lifeblood of the stock market.
High yields undercut the stock market in other ways too. When a Treasury is paying more in interest, that can draw investors away from investments that carry more risk. Why pay record prices for U.S. stocks when a U.S. government bond is paying more than before to wait in relative safety?
Gold, bitcoin and many other investments can also feel downward pressure from high yields.
When yields rise, the U.S. and other governments have to pay more in interest to cover their debts. That’s painful whendebt loads for governments worldwide are ballooningas they spend far more than they’re bringing in through revenue.
And if the U.S. government is already paying this much to borrow money when the economy is growing, what will happen if it needs to borrow even more to manage the pain when the next severe recession hits?
That’s why jumps in yields can scare politicians even more than swings in the stock market.
The bond market helped makeLiz Trussthe United Kingdom’s shortest-serving prime minister in 2022, whenit revolted against her planto cut taxes and raise spending without a way to pay for them.
Last year, President Donald Trump said thebond market may have played a rolein his decision to delay many of his proposed tariffs, saying that he noticed investors there “were getting a little queasy.”
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s move is a high-stakes effort to contain the rise in long-term yields, and some analysts are skeptical the impact will last.
“The operation changes almost nothing in terms of the fundamentals, in particular the unchanged need to finance the tidal wave of hyperscaler debt in addition to very large government deficits,” Krishna Guha, an analyst at Evercore ISI, and colleagues wrote in a note to clients.
“Hyperscalers” refers to the Big Tech companies that are borrowing mountains of money to build AI data centers. The bonds they’re selling are competing with U.S. Treasurys for buyers, which can push bond yields higher.
The U.S. government, meanwhile, continues to run its own large deficits regardless of what the Treasury Department does with its repurchases.
“The move could even backfire if the limited firepower results in little sustained impact,” Guha said.
The Federal Reserve could always cut the federal funds rate, which affects very short-term, overnight loans.
But longer-term yields like the 10- and 30-year Treasury yields are set by investors in the bond market. And recently, they have been demanding more in interest to make up for the growing risks of high inflation, continued government deficits and other factors.
The Fed also appears more likely to raise its benchmark short-term rate than to cut it. At its last meeting in late July, three Fed policymakersvoted to raise the fed funds rateseven as nine voted to keep it unchanged. And Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s decision to signal little about the Fed’s next moves appeared to push longer-term Treasury yields higher amid questions about what the central bank will do to get inflation back to its 2% target.
The government’s most recent inflation data suggest inflationmay be slowing, leading many on Wall Street to forecast the Fed will keep the federal funds rates steady at its next meeting in September. The next big potentially market-moving event may come on Aug. 28, when Warsh will give a speech at the Fed’s annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

item.title: 财政部采取行动缓解债券市场压力后，美股止住跌势
item.description:
NEW YORK (AP) — U.S. stocks rose Wednesday after the U.S. Treasury Department announced a move that could easepressure coming from the bond market. Strong profit reports for the spring from Estee Lauder,Targetand other U.S. companies also helped support Wall Street.
The S&P 500 climbed 0.2% for its first gainin four daysafter settingits all-time highlast week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 119 points, or 0.2%, and the Nasdaq composite ticked 0.2% higher.
Financial markets have come undergrowing strainas Treasury yields charged higher through the summer on worries aboutinflation, biggovernment debtsand other factors. That makesborrowing money more expensivefor everyone, which slows the economy and undercuts prices for stocks and other investments.
But Treasury yields fell in the morning after the U.S. Treasury Department said it will at least double the size of its planned purchases of longer-term Treasurys from Sept. 9 through Nov. 4. The department said it’s doing so “to provide greater liquidity support in longer-dated nominal sectors where there is consistent strong sponsorship from market participants.”
These longer-term 10- and 30-year Treasurys are less beholden to the Federal Reserve, which can raise or lower very short-term interest rates for overnight loans. President Donald Trump has lobbied for the Fed to lower interest rates to help the economy.
Longer-term yields are set instead by investors in the bond market, who decide how much interest they need to get paid by the U.S. government in exchange for lending it money. And recently, they have been demanding more in interest to make up for the growing risks of high inflation, continued government deficits and other factors.
After the Treasury department’s announcement, the yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.64% from 4.71% late Tuesday. It, though, remains well above its 3.97% level from before thewar with Iransent oil prices and worries about inflation much higher.
The 30-year Treasury yield, which recently touched its highest level since 2007, fell more sharply to 5.18% from 5.28% late Tuesday.
The relief could be short lived, some analysts warn. The amount of bonds the U.S. Treasury is proposing to repurchase is a fraction of the overall total.
“The boost to buybacks is also happening in a world of challenged Fed credibility,” according to strategists at BNP Paribas. Investors are questioning whether the Federal Reserve will raise the federal funds rate soon to match the tough talk its chairman, Kevin Warsh, has been offering on getting inflation down toward its 2% target.
“We do not believe buybacks will be enough to offset a continued loss in Fed credibility,” the BNP Paribas strategists wrote in a report, calling them “necessary, but not sufficient.”
On Wall Street, Moderna and Merck helped lead the market after they announced encouraging initial results from a study of a cancer vaccine they co-developed. The new drug showed better recurrence-free survival in melanoma patients who had a combination of it and Keytruda, a prescription immunotherapy drug made by Merck, than with Keytruda alone.
Moderna soared 177%, while Merck jumped 12.6%.
The continuing parade of U.S. companies reporting bigger profits for the spring than analysts expected, meanwhile, continues to support stocks.
Estee Lauder rallied 16.3% after CEO Stéphane de La Faverie said a key measure of its revenue growth accelerated for a fourth straight quarter. It reported growth in revenue around the world, with the strongest in mainland China.
The skin care company reported earnings per share of 39 cents, after excluding some restructuring and other one-time expenses. That’s up from just 9 cents a year earlier and was better than the 32 cents that analysts expected, according to FactSet.
Such growth is imperative because stock prices tend to follow the path of corporate profits over the long term. And strong growth helps allay criticism that stock prices shot too high in their runs to records.
Target rose 4.3%, Lowe’s added 2% and homebuilder Toll Brothers climbed 4% after they all reported better profits for the latest quarter than expected.
They helped offset drops for some Big Tech stocks, which restrained the overall market.
Broadcom fell 4.6% and was the heaviest weight on the S&P 500. It and other winners of theartificial-intelligenceboom have beenswingingsharplythrough the summeron worriesthat their stocks may have shot too high and that the AI frenzy may not be sustainable if it doesn’t produce big-enough profits.
All told, the S&P 500 rose 16.22 points to 7,707.98. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 119.65 to 53,463.05, and the Nasdaq composite added 41.38 to 26,331.09.
In stock markets abroad, indexes were mostly lower in Asia and mixed in Europe.
Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 sank 3.2%. South Korea’s Kospi, which has been home to some of the world’s sharpest swings because of its heavy reliance on AI stocks, slumped 5.8%.
AP Writers Michelle Chapman, Chan Ho-him, Mike Stobbe and Elaine Kurtenbach contributed to this report.
